reason: A NEW DEFECT CLASS FOR THIS CAMPAIGN: A DEFENSIVE DIVIDE-BY-ZERO GUARD THAT SILENTLY CHANGED THE PHYSICS. The Fortran writes the accretion ratios unguarded at :2143 and :2152 as min(max(0.0, qrs(i,k,2)/qci(i,k,1)), 1.). When qc == 0 and qs > 0 the division yields IEEE +Inf, max(0,Inf) is Inf, and the clamp returns 1.0. The native port guarded the division and returned 0.0 for that case, which is the OPPOSITE end of the clamp. It is invisible in psacw, gated on qc > qmin and so never reached with qc == 0, but nsacw is gated on nc > ncmin, which passes with qc == 0, and there the ratio is load-bearing. Fixed by reproducing the Fortran result without performing the division: qc > 0 takes the normal path, qc == 0 with qs > 0 returns 1.0, and the qc == 0 with qs == 0 case is unreachable by any consumer since every use is gated on qs > qcrmin, qg > qcrmin or qc > qmin. Keeping the division out preserves FP-exception-trapping builds. This is the inverse of the standing rule to restructure risky Fortran idioms rather than transliterate them: here the idiom WAS restructured, defensively, and that is what broke it.
